ledger.note: 552: Justinian's army lands in southern Spain. Athanagild's revolt against Agila I (550-551) brought an appeal to Justinian in autumn 551 or winter 552; 'The army was probably sent and landed in June or July' 552 and defeated Agila in August or September. The page doubts that Liberius led it and gives no boundary; 'Southern Baetica was Byzantine from Málaga to the mouth of the Guadalete'.

region.text: the Algarve, which Suintila 'seized' in 624 and Sisebut had not taken

ledger.note: The Algarve: bridging. The Suintila page says Suintila 'seized Algarve, which his predecessor had not taken' in 624, so it was Byzantine by then; no page opened says when it was taken, and the Spania page's extent does not name it. 552 is the province's founding year.

Early March 555: a Byzantine force from Italy lands at Cartagena. 'The page says the landing was violent'; Agila was assassinated in late March 555 and Athanagild became king. The page does not call Cartagena a city seized from the Visigoths in these words; the Visigothic holder is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the coast up to 'the mouth of the Guadalete', with Medina Sidonia

ledger.note: 572: Leovigild retakes Medina Sidonia. The page says 'Medina Sidonia was reconquered by Leovigild' in 572 and, through 'the treachery of an insider', around 570. The Suintila page lists 'Assidonia' among Sisebut's conquests; the coast of the Guadalete is not dated separately, but 'By 600, the province was mostly Málaga, Cartagena' and the Balearics.

region.text: Málaga and Cartagena, the two most important cities

ledger.note: 614: Sisebut attacks the province. The magister Caesarius, a patrician, 'made a peace treaty with Sisebut' in 614; 'Sisebut carried out two large expeditions against the Byzantines' in 614-615. The Sisebut page says only that he 'campaigned successfully against the remnants of Byzantine power in Spania' and names no cities.

By 619: Málaga and Cartagena are Visigothic. Bridging: 'Before 619: Sisebut conquered Málaga. Its bishop appears at the Second Council of Seville that year'; the Suintila page has Sisebut retaking 'Cartagena, Malaga, Sagunto, and Assidonia'; the Spania page says Sisebut 'probably' razed Cartagena and it 'never reappeared in Visigothic Spain'. No page dates Cartagena.

By 619: the fighting for Málaga and Cartagena ends. Bridging, as above: Málaga is 'before 619'; the page puts Suintila's campaign 'against the Romans' around 620 under Sisebut's orders (Suintila page).

region.text: the Algarve, which Suintila 'seized' in 624 and Sisebut had not taken

ledger.note: 624: Suintila takes the last Byzantine land. 'What Sisebut had begun by retaking Cartagena, Malaga, Sagunto, and Assidonia from the Byzantines, Suintila finished in 624'; he 'seized Algarve, which his predecessor had not taken'. The Spania page: 'By 624 the province was in Visigothic hands except the Balearics'; its footnote gives 625 (Collins) or 629 (Wallace-Hadrill) for the last vestiges.

wars.outcome: Athanagild's revolt against Agila I (550-551) led him to ask Justinian for help; the Byzantine army landed in 552 and defeated Agila; a force from Italy landed at Cartagena in March 555; Agila was killed in late March and Athanagild became king, the Byzantines keeping the southern coast.
wars.note: Athanagild's rising is dated 549 to 551 on the page.

wars.outcome: Leovigild retook Medina Sidonia in 572 and put down Córdoba's rebellion; Sisebut made two expeditions in 614-615 and had Málaga before 619; Suintila 'finished' the reconquest in 624 with the Algarve.
wars.note: The Sisebut page gives no dates and names no cities; the Suintila page names Cartagena, Málaga, Sagunto and Assidonia.

certainty.note: The province was a coastal strip that 'never extended very far inland'; no page gives a line. The Algarve and the coast between Málaga and Cartagena are the least certain parts.

notes: Written by eu-05-x (additions). Cliopatria has no row; slug free. Three pages opened. Not settled: (1) the Balearics 'formed part of Spania' (Spania page) but the exarchate-of-africa dossier (af-02-x) claims them from 591; the two dossiers overlap on the islands and Spania's shapes leave them out; (2) the Algarve (Suintila page only; confidence 1 before 624) and Sagunto (Suintila page; not drawn); (3) Medina Sidonia in 572 (Spania page) versus under Sisebut (Suintila page); (4) Baza and the coast between Málaga and Cartagena are not drawn; (5) the Spania page's footnote gives 625 or 629 for the last vestiges; (6) the capital is Málaga or Cartagena; (7) no area on any page. Ceuta belonged to Mauretania Secunda, not Spania (page).
